classification.difficultyReason: Students use the supplied parallel to justify the triangle sum through alternate angles and a straight angle, then extend the explicitly prompted quadrilateral triangulation to five triangles in a heptagon.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=180^{\circ}$; that is, that the sum of the angles in any triangle is $180^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal base and a supplied horizontal parallel through its upper vertex; matching right-pointing parallel marks and three interior angle labels.
spec.mathematics: The auxiliary line is parallel to the base. Interior angles are alpha, beta and gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied proof scaffolding is visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=180^{\circ}$.

Alternate angles on the supplied parallel lines place all three angles together on a straight line at the upper vertex.
answer.worked:
The angle between the upper line to the left and the left side of the triangle equals $\alpha$ (alternate angles, since the upper line is parallel to the base). The angle between the right side and the upper line to the right equals $\gamma$ for the same reason.

These two angles and $\beta$ form a straight angle at the upper vertex. Hence $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=180^{\circ}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By dividing the quadrilateral below into two triangles, show that the sum of the angles in a quadrilateral is $360^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Unshaded convex quadrilateral ABCD, with no supplied diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Boundary order A–B–C–D; interior remains available for drawing a diagonal.

answer.short:
$360^{\circ}$.

A diagonal divides the quadrilateral into two triangles.
answer.worked:
Draw diagonal $AC$, forming triangles $ABC$ and $ACD$. Each triangle has angle sum $180^{\circ}$ by part a. Together, their angles make exactly the four interior angles of the quadrilateral.

$$\text{Quadrilateral angle sum}=2\times180^{\circ}=360^{\circ}.$$

spec.description: Complete quadrilateral with the solution diagonal AC.
spec.mathematics: Diagonal AC partitions the quadrilateral into two triangles.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A heptagon is a seven-sided figure, as shown below. What is the angle sum of a heptagon?

spec.description: Unlabelled, unshaded convex irregular heptagon with seven sides.
spec.mathematics: Seven vertices and seven boundary edges; no supplied diagonals.

answer.short:
$900^{\circ}$.

Diagonals from one vertex divide the heptagon into five triangles.
answer.worked:
Draw diagonals from one vertex to its four non-adjacent vertices. This divides the heptagon into five triangles, whose angles together make its interior angles.

$$\text{Heptagon angle sum}=5\times180^{\circ}=900^{\circ}.$$
